```{r Data file}
Data <- read.csv("C:\\Users\\Olga_\\OneDrive\\Documents\\Olga Documents\\my projects and summary\\showcase tasks\\CLLT\\diabetes.csv",stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

df <- Data # work on df dataframe, Data stays compleet

# Here is the code to add the additional columns to df 
# Convert futime from days to years
df$futime_years <- df$futime / 365.25

# Re-specify data in rms format
dd <- datadist(df); options(datadist = "dd")

# Define the binary outcome: diabetes within 5 years
df$diabetes_5y <- ifelse(df$status == 1 & df$futime_years <= 5, 1, 0)
```


```{r Data exploration}
# Basic summary
cat("Total rows:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Duplicate rows:", sum(duplicated(df)), "\n\n")  # this works correctly on data frames

# Data type and missing value summary
summary_df <- data.frame(
  Column = names(df),
  DataType = sapply(df, class),
  MissingValues = sapply(df, function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
  IsDouble = sapply(df, function(x) is.double(x))
)

# Count missing values in weight, height, or bmi
missing_rows <- df[is.na(df$weight) | is.na(df$height) | is.na(df$bmi), ]

# Total rows with any missing in weight/height/bmi
n_missing <- nrow(missing_rows)

# Total number of rows in dataset
n_total <- nrow(df)

# Number of complete rows
n_complete <- n_total - n_missing

# Print summary
cat("Total rows:", n_total, "\n")
cat("Rows with any missing (weight/height/bmi):", n_missing, "\n")
cat("Rows with complete weight, height, and bmi:", n_complete, "\n")

Dup_df <- df[duplicated(df),]

print(summary_df)
print(Dup_df)
```


```{r Missing values NOT USED}
# Important note- I decided not to use imputed values since that may add inaccuracy later and the cohort is still large enough, but the code is still here to enable examine my way of thinking.
###
# Deal with missing values, missing values are numeric (integer and numeric)
# Many missing values in those columns, will not delete is because these rows or columns can be #lost for other attributes it they are deleted. 
#add additional df with imputed data in case it is needed in future
# No duplicated values

# Check missing data pattern
md.pattern(df)
# Perform imputation using predictive mean matching # using regression
imputed_data <- mice(df, method = "pmm", m = 5, seed = 123)
# Complete the data with the first imputed dataset
df_imputed <- complete(imputed_data, 1)
# Optional: View a summary
summary(df_imputed)


# Data type and missing value summary
summary_df_imputed <- data.frame(
  ColumnImput = names(df_imputed),
  DataTypeImput = sapply(df_imputed, class),
  MissingValuesImput = sapply(df_imputed, function(x) sum(is.na(x))),
  IsDoubleImput = sapply(df_imputed, function(x) is.double(x))
)

print(summary_df_imputed)
```

```{r Q1.a 5-year risk of developing diabetes }

# general KM model
# Fit the Kaplan-Meier model
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(futime_years, status) ~ 1, data = df)

## 5 years cumulative risk 

# Proportion diagnosed with diabetes within 5 years
km_summary <- summary(km_fit, times = 5)

# Survival probability and  95% CI
surv_5y  <- km_summary$surv                  
surv_5y_lower <- km_summary$lower           # Lower CI for S(5)
surv_5y_upper <- km_summary$upper           # Upper CI for S(5)

# Convert to cumulative incidence (1 - S(t))
risk_5y <- 1 - surv_5y
risk_5y_lower <- 1 - surv_5y_upper   # Note: upper survival = lower risk
risk_5y_upper <- 1 - surv_5y_lower   # Note: lower survival = upper risk

# Plot the KM curve (time to diabetes)
km_plot <- ggsurvplot(
  km_fit,
  xlab = "Years Since Pre-Diabetes Diagnosis",
  ylab = "Proportion Without Diabetes",
  title = "Kaplan-Meier Curve: Time to Diabetes Diagnosis",
  #surv.scale = "percent",
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.int.style = "ribbon",
  conf.int.alpha = 0.2,
  palette = c("#2E9FDF"),
  ggtheme = theme_classic(),
  break.x.by = 5,
  break.y.by = 0.2,           
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.title = "Patients at Risk",
  risk.table.y.text.col = TRUE,
  risk.table.height = 0.25,
  font.main = c(16, "bold"),
  font.x = c(14, "plain"),
  font.y = c(14, "plain"),
  font.tickslab = c(12, "plain"),
  risk.table.fontsize = 4,
  legend = "none"
)

# 5Y Proportion value annotation
#line
km_plot$plot <- km_plot$plot +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = surv_5y, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40")
# annotation
km_plot$plot <- km_plot$plot +
  annotate("text", x = max(km_fit$time) * 0.7, y = surv_5y + 0.03,
           label = paste0("~", round(surv_5y,2), " without DM at 5 years"),
           size = 4, color = "grey30")

print(km_plot)

# Print 
cat("Estimated 5-Year Risk of Diabetes:", round(risk_5y * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval:", round(risk_5y_lower * 100, 2), "% -", round(risk_5y_upper * 100, 2), "%\n")


# Pts censored before 5 years (status == 0)
censored_lt_5y <- df$status == 0 & df$futime_years < 5

# Total number of patients
total_patients <- nrow(df)

# Number and proportion of censored pts before 5 years
n_censored <- sum(censored_lt_5y)
prop_censored <- round(n_censored / total_patients * 100, 2)

# Print 
cat("Censored before 5 years:", n_censored, "\n")
cat("Total patients:", total_patients, "\n")
cat("Proportion censored before 5 years:", prop_censored, "%\n")
```


```{r Q1.b and 1.d factors associated with elevated risk and model performance score}

# Keeping only rows complete for variables used in the model
df_Cox_model <- df[complete.cases(df[, c("age", "male", "weight", "height", "bmi", "type")]), ]

# Fit Cox model with related variables
cox_model <- coxph(Surv(futime_years, status) ~ age + male + weight + height + bmi + type, data = df_Cox_model)

# View model summary
cox_sum <-summary(cox_model)
cox_sum

ggforest(cox_model, data = df_Cox_model)
```

```{r Q1.d alternative model - Logistic Regression}

#Data frame for the model, with complete case filtering

df_log_model <- df[complete.cases(df[, c("age", "male", "weight", "height", "bmi", "type", "diabetes_5y")]), ]


#logistic regression model

log_model <- glm(diabetes_5y ~ age + male + weight + height + bmi + type, 
                 data = df_log_model, family = "binomial")
summary(log_model)

# Tidy logistic regression output and exponentiation to get odds ratios
log_tidy <- tidy(log_model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)

ggplot(log_tidy[-1, ], aes(x = term, y = estimate)) +  # remove intercept
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  coord_flip() +
  ylab("Odds Ratio (95% CI)") +
  xlab("") +
  ggtitle("Logistic Regression: Odds Ratios for 5-Year Diabetes Risk") +
  theme_minimal()




# logistic model for patient number 1 (subject#1)

# Predict log-odds and standard error for subject #1
pt1_pred_logit <- predict(log_model, newdata = subject1, se.fit = TRUE, type = "link")

# Compute 95% CI on logit scale
logit_lower <- pt1_pred_logit$fit - 1.96 * pt1_pred_logit$se.fit
logit_upper <- pt1_pred_logit$fit + 1.96 * pt1_pred_logit$se.fit

# Transform to probability scale
prob_estimate <- plogis(pt1_pred_logit$fit)
prob_lower <- plogis(logit_lower)
prob_upper <- plogis(logit_upper)

# Print nicely
cat("Predicted 5-year risk:", round(prob_estimate * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(prob_lower * 100, 2), "% -", round(prob_upper * 100, 2), "%]\n")


## Logistic Model Estimation ROC and AUC

# Calculate ROC curve
roc_obj <- roc(df_log_model$diabetes_5y, predict(log_model, type = "response"))

# Plot with ggplot
ggroc(roc_obj) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  ggtitle("ROC Curve: Logistic Regression Model") +
  xlab("1 - Specificity") +
  ylab("Sensitivity") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = 0.1,
           label = paste("AUC =", round(auc(roc_obj), 3)),
           hjust = 0, size = 4.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

```{r Q1.g Treatment B}
### Q1.g is treatment B better than treatment A in preventing diabetes 
### Cox model for comparison by type (type A = 0, Type B = 1)

## KM model for comparison by type (treatment A and B)
km_fit_type <- survfit(Surv(futime_years, status) ~ type, data = df)

ggsurvplot(
  km_fit_type,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  pval = TRUE,
  xlab = "Years Since Pre-Diabetes Diagnosis",
  ylab = "Proportion Not Diagnosed with Diabetes",
  title = "Kaplan-Meier Curve by Treatment Type",
  legend.labs = c("Treatment A", "Treatment B"),
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.title = "Patients at Risk",
  risk.table.y.text.col = TRUE,
  risk.table.height = 0.3
)


survdiff(Surv(futime_years, status) ~ type, data = df)

# Adjusted cox model
cox_model_type <- coxph(Surv(futime_years, status) ~ type + age + male + weight + height + bmi, data = df_Cox_model)
summary(cox_model_type)
ggforest(cox_model_type, data = df_Cox_model)
```
